steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Globalisation is the increasing interconnection of world economies through trade, investment, and technology - it means businesses can operate internationally more easily.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Multinational corporations (MNCs) operate in multiple countries: they benefit from lower labour costs and new markets but face cultural differences and complex regulations.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Employment law protects workers: National Minimum Wage, Working Time Regulations, Health and Safety at Work Act, Equality Act (preventing discrimination).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Consumer protection legislation (Consumer Rights Act 2015) ensures products are as described, fit for purpose, and of satisfactory quality - giving consumers the right to refunds, repairs, or replacements.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain two benefits and two drawbacks of globalisation for a UK business. | Describe how the Consumer Rights Act 2015 protects customers and affects businesses. | Evaluate whether employment legislation does more harm than good to businesses.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: When discussing legislation, always identify WHO it protects and WHAT it costs businesses. Globalisation questions need a balanced answer: consider both UK businesses expanding abroad AND foreign businesses entering UK markets. Use specific legislation names (Consumer Rights Act, Equality Act) to show AO1 knowledge.
